note: Dates come from the election offices, the Federal Election Commission and the news sources linked on each entry. Ballot measures are listed by topic from Ballotpedia News coverage as of November 2, 2026; their titles are Ballotpedia’s, not always the official ballot titles. No source we read tied a state measure to a particular AAPI community, so no community positions are shown yet.

dates.t: General Election Day 2028 (derived from federal statute)
dates.n: 2 U.S.C. 7 sets election day as the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even-numbered years, which falls on Nov. 7 in 2028 (date derived, not printed).

measures.t: Repeal Top-Four Ranked-Choice Voting Initiative
measures.what: Would repeal Alaska's top-four primary and ranked-choice general election system.

measures.t: Citizenship Voting Requirement Initiative
measures.what: Citizen-initiated state statute that would limit voting eligibility in Alaska to U.S. citizens.

measures.t: Citizenship Voting Requirement Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would define voting eligibility in Arkansas based on U.S. citizenship.

measures.t: Require Certain School Districts to Spend 60% of Operational Spending on Direct Instruction Measure
measures.what: Would require large Arizona school districts to spend at least 60% of operational spending on direct instruction.

measures.t: Limit Local Tax Rate on Groceries to 2% of Base Price and Require Voter Approval to Increase Tax Rate Measure
measures.what: Would cap local tax rates on groceries in Arizona at 2% of the base price and require voter approval to raise them.

measures.t: Prohibit New Photo Traffic Enforcement Systems Measure
measures.what: Would bar new photo traffic enforcement systems in Arizona and require voter approval for local governments to keep existing ones.

measures.t: Prohibit Race- or Ethnicity-Based Preferential Treatment, Public Education Offices, and Disciplinary Policies Amendment
measures.what: Would bar Arizona government bodies, including schools, from race- or ethnicity-based preferential treatment and from using state funds for related offices or training.

measures.t: Voter Identification and Citizenship Voting Requirements Amendment
measures.what: Would limit voting to citizens, restrict foreign election contributions, require government ID to vote and allow ballots to be tabulated at the voting location.

measures.t: Veteran and Housing Assistance Programs Bond Measure
measures.what: Would authorize an $11.25 billion bond for veteran and housing assistance programs in California.

measures.t: Renew State Income Tax Increase for Education Funding Initiative
measures.what: Would make California's top marginal income tax rates permanent, with the revenue going mainly to K-12 schools.

measures.t: Second Mortgage Homebuyer Program and Revenue Bond Initiative
measures.what: Would create a second-mortgage homebuyer program in California funded by $25 billion in revenue bonds.

measures.t: Voter Identification, Citizenship Verification, and Registered Voter List Administration Initiative
measures.what: Would add voter identification requirements, require citizenship verification for voter registration, and change how registered-voter lists are administered in California.

measures.t: One-Time Wealth Tax for State-Funded Healthcare, Education, and Food Assistance Programs Initiative
measures.what: Would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of California billionaires, with revenue for Medi-Cal and other health coverage, K-14 education and food assistance.

measures.t: Prohibit New Taxes on Retirement Holdings, Personal Assets, and Savings and Limit Retroactive Taxes
measures.what: Would bar new California taxes on retirement holdings, personal assets and savings and limit certain retroactive taxes; it was put forward in response to the billionaire tax measure.

measures.t: Two-Thirds Vote Requirement for Local Special Tax Initiatives and Property Tax Initiative Prohibition Amendment
measures.what: Would require two-thirds voter approval for citizen-initiated local special taxes in California and prohibit property taxes created by initiative.

measures.t: Spending Requirements for Federally Qualified Health Centers Initiative
measures.what: Would require California's federally qualified health centers to spend at least 90% of annual revenue on mission-related purposes.

measures.t: TABOR Revenue Cap Increase for K-12 Education Measure
measures.what: Would let Colorado keep excess tax revenue equal to its K-12 spending and send at least half of the surplus plus 2% of that year's K-12 spending to schools.

measures.t: Require Voter Identification Number for Mail-In Ballots Initiative
measures.what: Would require mail-in voters in Colorado to provide an identification number along with their signature.

measures.t: Establish a Graduated Income Tax Amendment
measures.what: Would replace Colorado's flat 4.4% income tax with six brackets from 3.7% to 8.4% and remove the uniform-rate requirement from TABOR; competes with Initiative 232.

measures.t: Cap Individual and Corporate Income Tax at 4.4% Initiative
measures.what: Would cap Colorado individual and corporate income tax rates at 4.4% of federal taxable income; competes with the graduated income tax measure.

measures.t: Require Commission and Supreme Court Approval for Mid-Decade Congressional Redistricting Initiative
measures.what: Would require any mid-decade congressional redistricting plan in Colorado to be approved by the independent redistricting commission and the state Supreme Court.

measures.t: Homestead Tax Exemptions, Property Assessments, and Spending Restrictions Amendment
measures.what: Would raise Florida's non-school homestead exemption, lower the assessment-increase cap for non-homestead property to 5% and limit local property-tax spending; needs 60% approval.

measures.t: Increase Time for Senate to Act on Judicial Appointments Amendment
measures.what: Would extend from 30 to 60 days the time the Hawaii Senate has to act on certain judicial appointments made between April 1 and December 31.

measures.t: Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity (RISE) Bonds Amendment
measures.what: Would let Hawaii counties issue RISE bonds, repaid from real property tax revenue and exempt from debt limits, to finance public works and housing and community development.

measures.t: Bailable Offenses and Substantial Risk Standard Amendment
measures.what: Would allow Indiana courts to deny bail when evidence is strong and the accused poses a substantial risk to others or the community.

measures.t: Citizenship Voting Requirement Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would define voting eligibility in Kansas based on U.S. citizenship.

measures.t: Limit on Required Lot Size for Single-Family Homes Initiative
measures.what: Would limit local minimum lot-size requirements for single-family homes in Massachusetts.

measures.t: Permit Collective Bargaining for Committee for Public Counsel Services Employees Initiative
measures.what: Would allow collective bargaining for employees of the Massachusetts public defender agency.

measures.t: Change State Tax Revenue Limit Initiative
measures.what: Would change how the Massachusetts state tax revenue limit is calculated and count the tax on income above $1 million toward state tax revenue.

measures.t: Top-Two Primary Elections Initiative
measures.what: Would create top-two primaries for Massachusetts state offices and require joint gubernatorial and lieutenant gubernatorial primary tickets.

measures.t: Permit Same-Day Voter Registration Initiative
measures.what: Would establish same-day voter registration in Massachusetts.

measures.t: Provide That Nothing in State Constitution Establishes Criteria for Congressional Redistricting Amendment
measures.what: Would limit the constitution's contiguity, compactness and equal-population criteria to legislative districts and let the legislature give the state Supreme Court original jurisdiction over congressional map challenges.

measures.t: Congressional Map Referendum
measures.what: Referendum on a congressional map in Missouri; Ballotpedia reported it as newly certified for the November ballot in mid-September 2026.

measures.t: Amendment to keep judicial elections nonpartisan
measures.what: Citizen-initiated constitutional amendment that would keep Montana's judicial elections nonpartisan.

measures.t: Require Voter Identification Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment on voter identification requirements, one of six statewide voter ID measures Ballotpedia counts for 2026.

measures.t: Require Voter Identification Initiative
measures.what: Citizen-initiated measure that would require voter identification in Nevada elections.

measures.t: Require Voter Identification Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment (SJR 10) setting voter ID requirements, including photo ID for in-person voting.

measures.t: Higher Education Facilities Bond Measure
measures.what: Would authorize $275 million in bonds for Rhode Island higher education facilities, part of five bond questions totaling $600 million.

measures.t: Housing Development Bond Measure
measures.what: Would authorize $120 million in bonds to build and preserve affordable and accessible housing in Rhode Island.

measures.t: Citizenship Voting Requirement Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would define voting eligibility in South Dakota based on U.S. citizenship.

measures.t: Remove Right to Bail for Certain Criminal Offenses Measure
measures.what: Would remove the right to bail in Tennessee for certain serious offenses when guilt is presumed strongly, such as terrorism and second-degree murder.

measures.t: Remove Constitutional Same-Sex Marriage Ban Amendment
measures.what: Would remove the same-sex marriage ban from Virginia's constitution.

measures.t: Voting Rights Restoration for Felons Upon Release Amendment
measures.what: Would amend Virginia's constitution to restore voting rights to people with felony convictions upon release.

measures.t: Right to Collective Bargaining Amendment
measures.what: Would add a right to collective bargaining to Vermont's constitution.

measures.t: Equal Protection of Law Amendment
measures.what: Would add that people are guaranteed equal protection under the law and bar denying rights based on race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or national origin.

measures.t: Repeal Tax on Household Income Over $1 Million and Prohibit State and Local Taxes on Income Initiative
measures.what: Would repeal Washington's tax on household income over $1 million and prohibit state and local taxes on income.

measures.t: Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred amendment to Wisconsin's constitution on government discrimination and preferential treatment; Ballotpedia classes it among 2026 constitutional-rights measures.

measures.t: Citizenship Voting Requirement Amendment
measures.what: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would define voting eligibility in West Virginia based on U.S. citizenship.

measures.t: Homeowner's Primary Residence Property Tax Exemption Measure
measures.what: Would exempt half of the assessed value of a primary residence from Wyoming property tax.
